summary:
South Dakota stands under the United States national framework, and that framework is the sharpest exposure for a trans visitor. Executive Order 14168, signed 20 January 2025, redefined sex for federal purposes as a male-female binary, barred transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with their gender identity, prohibited self-selection of gender on passports and visas, and directed the attorney general to "correct the misapplication" of Bostock v. Clayton County (2020). The State Department stopped processing the X marker and any marker not matching sex assigned at birth; new passport applications are processed only as M or F according to supporting documents, and passports already issued with an X marker remain valid until they expire. The Supreme Court in November 2025 allowed the passport sex-marker restrictions to take effect, superseding a State Department policy in place since 1992. Trans and nonbinary travellers report passports confiscated or blocked at application, with some left stranded abroad; the ACLU has sued the State Department on behalf of seven plaintiffs, and Lambda Legal maintains guidance on what documentation to consider and how name and gender changes interact with federal records.

Screening at US checkpoints carries an outing risk: TSA procedures can involve secondary screening, devices and pat-downs that are invasive of privacy. Several governments have responded to the document and data rules. In April 2025 CNN reported that several countries issued advisories about trans people travelling to the United States, and Axios reported in March 2025 that at least eight European countries, including Finland and Denmark, adjusted travel guidelines for trans and nonbinary citizens entering the country.

Within South Dakota itself, facility access is now restricted by statute. Governor Larry Rhoden's office announced on 21 March 2025 that he had signed House Bill 1259 the previous day, limiting restrooms, locker rooms and changing areas in public schools and state-owned buildings to a person's sex, effective 1 July 2025. It is the first measure of its kind to enter the South Dakota code, after comparable legislation failed in 2016, 2017, twice in 2018 and in 2022. The bill passed the state House 49-21 and reaches state-run facilities broadly, primarily K-12 schools and state colleges, including off-campus activities, and prisons.

A July 2026 anti-trans legal-risk assessment for transgender travellers, built on five years of daily legislative tracking and a rubric identifying the most damaging bills, lists South Dakota among the worst states for legislation targeting transgender adults; it reports that federal policies continue to create legal difficulties for transgender people nationwide.

Elsewhere in the national framework, federal custody and care present documented harm. From 2026 the Federal Bureau of Prisons adopted Florida-based policies mandating conversion therapy for transgender inmates, including cutting hair short, withdrawing hormone medication and substituting psychiatric therapy and drugs; the Bureau stopped reporting the number of transgender prisoners held from 2025. In ICE custody, transgender men were reportedly subjected to forced-labour programmes, with refusals met by beatings, solitary confinement and reports of severe sexual abuse. In December 2025 the Attorney General instructed the FBI to offer cash bounties for information leading to the identification and arrest of transgender activists described as promoting "radical gender ideology" and characterised as "domestic terrorist groups"; a May 2026 White House counterterrorism strategy stated that activities would prioritise the identification and neutralisation of groups whose ideology is "anti-American, radically pro-transgender, and anarchist." Advocates have compared these actions to the early stages of genocide.

Care access is constrained. Executive Order 14187 (January 2025) described gender-affirming care for minors as "chemical and surgical mutilation of children," leading some hospitals to pause care; in summer 2025 the Department of Justice subpoenaed over 20 hospitals for full records of patients under 19. In July 2025 the federal government shut down specialised LGBTQ youth services on the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, and October 2025 proposed rules would bar Medicaid reimbursement for care to transgender patients under 18. Gender-affirming care for children is already banned in 27 states. Several of these federal measures have been blocked or enjoined in court.

Visa screening carries its own exposure. In February 2025 the State Department announced a ban on trans athletes entering the US to compete in women's sports, flagging visa applicants with an internal marking and treating applicants who list a gender other than their assigned sex as grounds for a permanent ban on grounds of fraud.
tangentialFactors:
The Movement Advancement Project tally places the South Dakota statute within a wider pattern: state bathroom bans applying to trans people in K-12 schools and some government buildings cover nine states and one territory, with outright state bans on facility use per gender identity in additional states, while 29 states, four territories and the District of Columbia have no such ban. Some states make trans bathroom use a criminal offence in certain circumstances. In April 2025 a transgender student was arrested and handcuffed in a women's restroom at the Florida state capitol, which civil-rights attorneys described as the first known arrest under that state's bathroom-restriction law.

South Dakota's facility law arrived late relative to its neighbours in the legislative cycle. Similar bills failed in the state in 2016, 2017, twice in 2018 and in 2022, and the 2025 measure is the first of its kind on the state's books.

Other states have moved further on documents. In February 2026 Kansas enacted a law preventing transgender people from changing markers on birth certificates and driver's licences and invalidating existing documents that do not match sex assigned at birth, and barring trans people from sex-segregated facilities; rights groups call it a template for other states, with further targeting bills pending in state legislatures. A July 2026 national risk assessment flagged Idaho as the latest "Do Not Travel" state for trans people, bringing the total to four states so flagged, and reported that the 2026 legislative season continued to degrade trans rights while federal policies drove nationwide trends.

Several federal measures remain contested. The ACLU's suit against the State Department is pending on behalf of seven plaintiffs, and a number of the federal care and funding measures have been blocked or enjoined in court.
localsOnly:
House Bill 1259 applies to people using restrooms, locker rooms and changing areas in public schools and state-owned buildings, with state-run facilities including K-12 schools, state colleges and off-campus activities in its scope. It took effect on 1 July 2025.

The bill's "reasonable accommodation" clause and the House floor debate raised the prospect that incarcerated trans people would be placed in solitary confinement in order to comply with the facility restriction, and the reporting on the measure identifies prisons as within its institutional reach.

The measure cleared the state House 49-21 before the governor's signature on 20 March 2025, announced by his office the following day.

Residents also stand under the federal regime described in the summary: birth-certificate and driver's licence markers in South Dakota, hate-crime coverage for trans victims, and state-level restrictions on gender-affirming care for minors are not addressed by the sources assembled for this record.
outOfScopeNotes:
No source in this inventory states South Dakota's rules for changing sex markers on birth certificates or driver's licences, or whether documents issued with a non-matching marker are recognised. That question is unresolved here.

The inventory does not establish whether South Dakota provides hate-crime or penalty-enhancement protection covering anti-trans violence, nor whether any such provision has been enforced.

Whether South Dakota is one of the four states flagged "Do Not Travel" in the July 2026 assessment is not sourced; that assessment is reported to list South Dakota among the worst states for legislation targeting transgender adults, which is a separate categorisation.

The sources do not confirm whether South Dakota bans gender-affirming care for minors; the count of 27 states with such a ban is not broken down by state here.

Which of the federal measures described have been blocked or enjoined, and whether any enjoined relief reaches a visitor in South Dakota, is unresolved in this inventory.
